messages:
IncidentBot: ALERT: sustained spike observed for model family sylph7b — rolling 10m TPM = 6.2k (threshold 3k). Auto-sculpt applied to free tier. Paging oncall.
Samir: oncall — seeing queue growth and elevated latency, several 429s from customers. dashboards: https://dash.internal/sylph7b
Maria: thanks. is this traffic organic or attacky? any anomalous prompt shapes?
Jordan: runtime: traffic is legitimate (high completion length + streaming-heavy). KV cache hit dropped. We can enforce a per-family TPM cap immediately from routing layer.
Samir: ok plan proposal: 1) set sylph7b global TPM cap to 2100 2) carve out enterprise reserved capacity (keep current) 3) route excess to sylph7b-quant fallback and guppy-medium 4) notify CS and status page. Thoughts?
Maria: +1. prefer 2100 rather than blunt 50% cut so critical customers stable. also enable temporary higher RPM per-customer to avoid short-burst 429s for logged-in apps.
Jordan: I can apply TPM change now. internal API:
```
curl -X POST "https://admin.internal/api/v1/ratelimits" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model_family":"sylph7b","limit_type":"tpm","value":2100,"scope":"global","note":"auto mitigation - oncall Samir"}'
```
Samir: do it. also add a per-customer RPM floor so existing sessions don't cut mid-stream. set rpm_floor=60 for enterprise keys.
Jordan: applying TPM cap... OpsBot: deploying new rate limit config to routing-prod..
OpsBot: SUCCESS: rate limit applied (sylph7b tpm=2100). routing change pushed to 4 regions.
Samir: seeing immediate drop in backend queue length and tail latency. 429s down but some edge clients still hitting client-side throttles.
CS Team: ping — we have 3 customer tickets mentioning errors. pls confirm which customers are carved out. list: acme-inc, big-retailer.
Samir: acme-inc + big-retailer are on reserved capacity and unaffected. putting a short KB note now: https://wiki.internal/kb/sylph7b-rate-mitigation
Maria: runtime note: if we see re-rise within 30m, escalate to reduce global to 1600 and enable prefer-quant routing by default.
Jordan: adding prefer-quant routing: route_ratio(sylph7b->sylph7b-quant)=0.25 for new requests.
Samir: leaving detailed handoff for Kai (night). docs: what we changed, rollback command, graphs links.
Samir: Handoff in 25m to @Kai — please monitor errors per-customer and tail p99 latency, rollback plan in 3h if stable.
Kai: ack. I'll watch p95/p99, error budget, and set a timed rollback in 3h if no regressions. thanks for the notes.
OpsBot: INCIDENT NOTE: mitigation applied by Jordan (oncall). change-id: rl-98765.
Maria: FYI we also added a short-lived alert: "sylph7b_tpm_headroom < 20%" to avoid oscillation.
Samir: CS updated public status with advisory about degraded responses for heavy streaming workloads and recommended fallbacks.
IncidentBot: MONITORING: aggregate TPM decreased to 1.9k after mitigation; p99 latency improved.
Kai: saw a small blip after config propagation, stabilized. keeping prefer-quant at 25% for 2h.
Samir: after 2.5h traffic normalized and error rate back to baseline. I'm going to revert to previous TPM (3500) in 10m and remove prefer-quant.
Jordan: rolling revert now... OpsBot: SUCCESS: rate limit reverted (sylph7b tpm=3500), prefer-quant removed.
IncidentBot: RESOLVED: incident closed. total duration ~2h30m. follow-up: engineering to add longer-term KV cache warmup and consider a persistent fallback policy for streaming-heavy workloads.
Kai: following up during next shift with post-incident notes and runbook updates.
Samir: thanks team — leaving a concise postmortem draft in #postmortems. :thumbsup:
